newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Syria says Turkey's Iraq operation an "invasion".
newsitem.headline: Syria says Turkey's Iraq operation an "invasion".

text.p: Syria's Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam tagged Turkey's military operation in northern Iraq as "an invasion and an occupation," Kuwait's news agency said on Monday.

"It is an invasion and an occupation of Arab territory. It is a dangerous matter regardless of our view about any regime in the Arab world," the official Kuwait News Agency quoted Khaddam as saying, during a short visit to the Gulf Arab state.
Syria, which took part in the 1991 U.S.-led coalition that ejected Iraqi troops from Kuwait, has had no diplomatic ties with Baghdad for almost two decades.
Several thousand Turkish troops, backed by tanks and heavy artillery, pushed across the border into northern Iraq on Wednesday in a sweep against separatist Kurdish rebel bases.
Ankara and Damascus have long been at odds over Syria's alleged support for the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel group and sharing the waters of the Euphrates river.

"The circumstances that the Arab nation is undergoing are difficult and complicated," said Khaddam. "There are incidents that emerge everyday that require (Arab) consultation and exchange of views," he added.
Khaddam, who is accompanied by Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, met with the Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah and handed him a message from Syria's President Hafez al-Assad.
